 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Azam @ Ajam Pasha, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 14.05.2024 at about 12.15 to 12.20 a.m (midnight), the said Azam @ Azam Pasha was proceeding in Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-04-JX-4089, proceeding from Doddaballapura to Bengaluru, driven by said Azam @ Azam Pasha and when he reached (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 near U turn Daba, Marasandra,
Doddaballapura - Bengaluru Road, at the same time the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-43-A-3365 belonging to the respondent No.1 who was proceeding in front of the said Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner, with excessive speed without giving any signal and suddenly applied brake, due to which the said Azam @
Ajam Pasha could not control the vehicle and dashed against the said Motor Cycle to back side of the said tipper lorry.

Due to which he fell down on the road along with Motor Cycle and sustained head and other grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Doddaballapura Government hospital for treatment,
but he died on the way to hospital.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of deadbody, funeral and obsequies.

Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and working as Welder at KF Kitchen Solutions, Peenya 2nd Stage, Bengaluru and earning more than Rs.40,000/-
p.m.

Due to untimely death of the deceased has badly affected the income of the deceased since he was the only bread earning member in their family and the petitioner is facing acute financial crunch and lost her (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 beloved son in her old age and also love and affection.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Tipper Lorry and in this regard the Rajanukunte Police have registered a case against driver of the offending Tipper Lorry.

The respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- to the petitioner with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. Respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending tipper lorry, age, avocation, income of the Shabeena vs Nanjundeswara Enterprises on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194197660/
2 deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, dependency of the petitioner with the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties and there is a delay of 3 (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 days in lodging the complaint and the offending tipper lorry was not at all responsible for the cause of accident and admits that this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in respect of the offending Tipper Lorry which was valid as on the date of accident and the liability if any is subject to terms, limitations and conditions of the policy and the rider of the Motor Cycle without wearing helmet and without a valid and effective driving licence ride the same on the date of accident.

The driver of the tipper lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and there is no valid RC, FC and Permit to the tipper lorry and hence there is a breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the owner.

The compensation claimed is excessive,
exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioner proves that she is the LR/dependent of deceased Sri.Azam @
Azam Pasha S/o Zabi?

Whether petitioner proves that deceased Sri.Azam @ Azam Pasha S/o Zabi was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 14.05.2024 at about 12.20 a.m, on Doddaballapura - Bengaluru Main Road, near U-turn Daba, Marasandra Village, Hesaraghatta, Yelahanka Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing registration No.KA-43-A-3365 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
06. In order to prove her case, the petitioner was got examined herself as PW.1 and got examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 23 documents as Ex.P.1 to 23 and closed her side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 got examined its Deputy Manager as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard both sides.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-

3  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3755/2024  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 :
As per final order  for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
Petitioner filed affidavit stated that, she is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the said fact, she has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of herself and deceased as per Ex.P.13 and 14 which shows that the petitioner is mother of the deceased.
There is no dispute in her cross-examination regarding relationship of the petitioner with the deceased.
So on perusal of these documents, it is true that the petitioner is the legal representative and dependent on the deceased.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner got herself examined as PW.1 and she has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 the offending tipper lorry by its driver, the accident took place and deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the way to hospital.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Rajanukunte Police against driver of the offending tipper lorry.
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending tipper lorry, the accident took place and deceased sustained injuries.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident on Bengaluru - Doddaballapura Main Road near U turn Daba,
Marasandra Village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending tipper lorry.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending tipper lorry has stated that one Allasa Yamanappa Kavadi Matti was driving the lorry at the time of accident and he had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident and said offending lorry had valid insurance policy as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.7 and 8 are IMV reports which discloses that both vehicles are involved in the accident and both vehicles got damaged.
Ex.P.9 is Inquest panchanama of deceased (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 Azam @ Azam Pasha.

Ex.P.10 is Post mortem report of deceased Azam @
Azam Pasha shows the cause of death is due to shock due to head injury leading to cardio vascular arrest.
Ex.P.11 is the important document of Investigation Officer.

After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending tipper lorry for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 304(A) of IPC and Ex.P.12 is Statement of eye-witnesses.
12. To disprove the petitioner case, RW.1 filed affidavit and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the written statement averments.

During her cross-examination she admits that as on Shabeena vs Nanjundeswara Enterprises on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194197660/
4 the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending lorry was in force and denied to the suggestion that after investigation the Police have filed Charge sheet against their insured lorry and they have not challenged Charge sheet anywhere and she has produced Authorization letter, Letter send to owner of the vehicle, Postal receipt and copy of Policy as per Ex.R.1 to 4 and as per Ex.R.4 as on the date of accident the policy of the offending lorry is valid and is in force.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the accident has (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending tipper lorry and deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the way to the hospital.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Azam @ Azam Pasha, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner has stated in her petition that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and working as Welder and earning more than Rs.40,000/- p.m and she has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of deadbody, funeral and obsequies.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner lost her loving son who is only bread earning member of the family and undergoing loss of pain and agony at her old age.
14. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioner has not produced any birth certificate, school records of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, she has produced Aadhaar card of the deceased as per Ex.P.13.

Eventhough the said (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1999.
The alleged accident occurred on 14.05.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 25 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 25 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is "18".
15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.15 Salary certificate of deceased and got examined Proprietor of KF Kitchen Solutions in which deceased was working as PW.2 and he has stated that deceased was employee of their company since 5 years and working as Welder and was drawing salary of Rs.20,000/- p.m and he was paid Rs.5,000/- for over time duty and he has produced his ID card, his Aadhaar card, Registration certificate and Registration (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 certificate of establishment, MSME certificate, Statement of account issued by Canara Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank and Certificate U/Sec 65B of Evidence Act as per Ex.P.16 to 22.

In his cross-examination PW.2 has stated that the drawing salary of the deceased is shown in bank statement and admits that on 16.12.2023 Rs.17,439/- was paid through Phonepay and said amount is not written as salary and he has paid Rs.20,000/- as salary and Rs.5,000/- as butta to the deceased and he has not produced any voucher, ledger extract regarding cash payment and he has income tax assessee and in IT returns it is not shown the salary of Rs.20,000/- is paid to Ajam Pasha.

Hence, in the absence of voucher and Shabeena vs Nanjundeswara Enterprises on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194197660/
5 ledger extract, IT returns regarding payment of salary to the deceased, considering the cross- examination of PW.2, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.20,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
16.
In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner is the mother of the deceased and she is the dependent on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

Since deceased was aged aged 25 years and was self employee at the time of accident, 40% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (20,000 + 8,000) = Rs.28,000/-.

It is also evident that in the present case the petitioner is the only one dependent and hence 50% of the income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (28,000 - 14,000) = Rs.14,000/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.14,000/-.
As the deceased was aged about 25 years, the multiplier of 18 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.30,24,000/- (Rs.14,000 x 12 x 18) towards loss of dependency.

17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
18. The claimant is the mother of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioner would be entitled for Rs.48,400/- towards loss of filial consortium and petitioner is entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 50% of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case

2. Loss of filial consortium 48,400-00 (For petitioner) (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3755/2024 3. Loss of estate 19,500-00 4.

6 19. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,11,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed objections and contested the matter by examining RW.1, but not proved its contentions.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount to the petitioner within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.3 partly in affirmative.
Issue No.4:-

In view of reasons assigned to above Issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 are partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,11,400/- (Rupees Thirty one lakhs eleven thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner being the mother of the deceased, on deposit of the compensation amount with interest, she is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
